points: Naomi had a kinsman of her husband, a mighty man of wealth of the family of Elimelech, and his name was Boaz.

note.label: Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz

points: Boaz answered that it had fully been shewed him all she had done for her mother in law since the death of her husband, how she left her father, her mother, and the land of her nativity, and came unto a people she knew not before.

note.label: Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz

points: At mealtime Boaz told her to come and eat of the bread and dip her morsel in the vinegar; he reached her parched corn, and she did eat and was sufficed and left.

note.label: Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz

points: When she rose to glean, Boaz commanded his young men to let her glean even among the sheaves without reproach, and to let fall handfuls of purpose for her. She gleaned until evening and beat out about an ephah of barley.

note.label: Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz

points: Ruth brought what she had gleaned into the city, gave Naomi what she had reserved, and told her, The man's name with whom I wrought to day is Boaz.

note.label: Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz

points: Naomi told her it was good to go out with his maidens, that they meet thee not in any other field; so Ruth kept fast by the maidens of Boaz to glean unto the end of barley harvest and of wheat harvest, and dwelt with her mother in law.

note.label: Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz

points: Ruth did according to all her mother in law bade her. When Boaz had eaten and drunk and his heart was merry, he lay down at the end of the heap of corn, and she came softly, uncovered his feet, and laid her down. At midnight the man was afraid, turned himself, and behold, a woman lay at his feet.

note.label: Ruth 3: The Skirt of the Near Kinsman

points: Boaz went up to the gate, called the kinsman of whom he had spoken to turn aside and sit down, and took ten men of the elders of the city to sit with them.
Boaz was not the closest kinsman, so he asked the nearer one first: if you redeem it, you must also take Ruth and raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: The elders blessed Boaz's house to be like the house of Pharez whom Tamar bare unto Judah; Pharez is his own ancestor, so the blessing is on the line.
Boaz went in unto her and the Lord gave her conception; that is what happens when a man goes in unto a woman, and by the Christian reading the Lord would have lain with Ruth.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife; and when he went in unto her, the Lord gave her conception, and she bare a son.
Raising up seed does not give a child two fathers; the record says Boaz begat Obed, not Mahlon, because Mahlon was dead.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: Generation goes back to genes and genealogy: Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar, Phares begat Esrom, down to Naasson, Salmon, Booz of Rachab, Obed of Ruth, Jesse and David the king.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: Boaz begat Obed of Ruth is where levirate marriage actually shows up, but we will not be bamboozled by a spin move into an Old Testament law that has nothing to do with the question asked.
